history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this record is the same famous temple as seq 1075 (id annapurna-devi-mandir-varanasi) - consider deduping the CSV rows. The temple stands ~15 metres northwest of the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Visheshwarganj/Vishwanath Gali; the present Nagara-style structure was built in 1729 CE by Maratha Peshwa Baji Rao I. It honours Annapurna, the provider of food: legend says Parvati withdrew all food after Shiva called the world illusion, then appeared as Annapurna to feed creation, establishing her cosmic kitchen at Kashi (she is called Kashipuradheshvari, Queen of Kashi, and is described in the Kashi Khanda of the Skanda Purana). The shrine houses a brass idol worshipped daily and a gold idol of the goddess (with a golden pot and ladle, flanked by Lakshmi and Bhudevi) shown only for four days a year from Dhanteras to Annakoot, when coins (khazana) and rice are distributed as prasad. The temple runs a free bhojanalaya (annadanam) for pilgrims and the needy daily. An ancient idol stolen in 1913 was being repatriated from Canada (verify).

name: Annapurna Devi Temple
town_description: Varanasi (Kashi/Banaras) is one of the world's oldest living cities, on the west bank of the Ganga in Uttar Pradesh. The spiritual capital of Hinduism, it is dominated by the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, the ghats (notably Dashashwamedh and Manikarnika), and institutions like Banaras Hindu University. It is a perennial pilgrimage centre for moksha-seeking Hindus and a hub of classical music, silk weaving and boat-based tourism.
